Predict one participant's free-text answer in a postgame questionnaire. The participant has finished an online public-goods game and is being debriefed. Initially four anonymous people formed a group. Before playing they took ten three-option questions about social groups; the top quiz scorer was publicly congratulated and marked with stars, but actual quiz scores were never disclosed. In each game round, each player received 10 lab-money points and chose an integer donation from 0 to 10 to a shared pot. In the ordinary version, the pot was doubled and divided equally among the players; a player's round earnings were their retained points plus their share. In the threshold version, if the pot was below 10, everyone's entire round earnings were zero, including retained points; otherwise the ordinary calculation applied. A donation had a 15-second window, after which the program chose a random amount automatically. The game actually ran six rounds, although the total was not announced beforehand. In one feedback condition, only own round earnings were shown; in the other, after each round a table showed IDs, donations, cumulative scores, average donation, the cumulative leader and the starred quiz leader. Group attrition occurred; exact individual histories and runtime handling are unavailable here. Completion paid at least US$1 with up to US$3 additional score-dependent bonus; no exact point-to-cash conversion is supplied.
The current task is an unrestricted text response, not a donation, a quiz answer, a correctness test or a researcher-assigned theme. The perceived-norm question asks what most people would say the participant should do; the explanation question asks why the participant acted as they did. They are distinct reports, neither is an objectively verified strategy. Predict only the requested answer from the available context. Output only the participant's original English response as a text string, with no translation, theme label, correction, explanation or quotation wrapper.
